_comment: Machine-readable editorial rules for every learner language. Read by the
translation pipeline (scripts/translation-*), by translation agents as the
style contract for a batch, and by translation-semantics QA. `script` names
the Unicode ranges a translation must be written in; `terminal` the
sentence-final punctuation convention observed in the shipping rows;
`secondPerson` and `register` the address policy the existing 600-word band
established. Rules of the invariant kind (never invent a subject, gender or
number Korean does not state) live in every entry because every language is
exposed to them. None of this is native review; see LOCALIZATION_NATIVE_REVIEW.md.

_invariants.neverInvent: If the Korean names no subject, gender, plural or possessor, the translation must not invent one unless the grammar of the language forces a choice; then prefer the construction that adds the least (subjectless, impersonal, or the Korean sentence's own topic).
_invariants.taughtSenseOnly: Translate the canonical taught sense the card carries, never another dictionary reading of the same spelling.
_invariants.koreanMeaningFirst: Translate the Korean sentence's meaning; the English row is a disambiguator, not the source. Do not copy English word order, articles or idioms into the target language.
_invariants.noKorean: Meanings and example translations carry no Hangul; a More-about-it note may name Korean words.
_invariants.noEnglish: No English words except true loanwords the language itself uses.

ar.secondPerson: أنتَ/أنتِ avoided; imperative polite forms as in the shipping rows
traps: do not drift into Egyptian/Levantine colloquialisms
verbal nouns for Korean nominalisations

bn.secondPerson: আপনি when Korean is polite, আমি first person as shipped
traps: danda । not period
do not calque English progressive

cs.secondPerson: vy for polite Korean, consistent with shipping rows
traps: aspect choice must follow Korean completedness
no anglicised word order

el.secondPerson: εσείς for polite, εσύ only where Korean is casual
traps: Greek question mark is the semicolon ;
gendered articles: prefer plural or impersonal when Korean names nobody

fil.secondPerson: kayo/po for Korean 해요체, as the shipping rows do
fil.register: po/opo politeness where Korean is polite
traps: keep po particles consistent
no deep Tagalog nobody speaks; no pure English substitutions
danda । not period
gender agreement of verbs: prefer constructions that avoid inventing the speaker's gender (e.g. करना चाहिए, हो गया)

hu.secondPerson: ön for polite; shipping rows use ön
traps: definite vs indefinite conjugation
no pro-drop violation — Hungarian drops subjects naturally, keep it
no Malay-specific vocabulary
saya not aku for the polite register

it.secondPerson: lei for polite, tu only where Korean is casual; shipping rows lean impersonal
traps: gendered participles: prefer constructions that avoid inventing gender (si impersonale, plural)
Kazakh-specific letters ә ғ қ ң ө ұ ү һ і must appear where the word needs them — their absence signals Russian leakage
no Russian loan where a Kazakh word is normal
Kyrgyz ң ө ү must appear where needed; watch Kazakh/Russian bleed-through
Mongolian ө ү must appear where needed
vowel harmony in suffixes

nl.secondPerson: u for polite Korean, as shipped
traps: no Flemish-only vocabulary
keep u consistent — no drift to je mid-pack

pl.secondPerson: pan/pani for polite Korean, as shipped
traps: aspect must follow Korean completedness
past-tense gender: prefer constructions avoiding an invented speaker gender where natural
comma-diacritics ș ț not cedilla ş ţ
aspect must follow Korean completedness
past-tense gender: prefer constructions avoiding an invented speaker gender (у меня..., мне...) where natural

sv.secondPerson: du (modern Swedish default), ni only in fixed polite formulas
traps: en/ett agreement
no Danish/Norwegian bleed
formal written verb endings as shipped
no Sri Lankan/colloquial mix
keep the shipped polite verb endings (-ండి for requests)

th.secondPerson: คุณ; polite particles as shipped (ครับ/ค่ะ omitted in neutral teaching rows)
th.register: neutral polite, ฉัน first person as shipped
traps: no sentence-final period
spaces only between clauses, not words
dotted/dotless i must be right
evidential -miş only when Korean implies hearsay
і/и/ї correct; no Russian lexical bleed (місто not город)
aspect follows Korean completedness
Latin Uzbek with oʻ/gʻ written as o' g' apostrophe forms as shipped
no Cyrillic
singular they for unnamed third persons
no gloss may smuggle a second dictionary sense
글자=letter, 음절=block, 단어=word — the fixed terminology

ja.question: ？or 。per shipped rows
traps: no invented subjects — Japanese drops them like Korean
kanji per shipped usage

zh-CN.secondPerson: 你 neutral, 您 only for explicit deference
traps: no traditional characters
full-width punctuation

es.secondPerson: usted/tú per shipped rows; keep consistent
traps: opening ¿ required
gendered participles: prefer impersonal where Korean names nobody
il impersonal only for weather/time — otherwise no invented il/elle
espace before ? per shipped rows: follow existing pack

de.secondPerson: du — the product addresses the learner as du everywhere; Sie only inside quoted formal speech
traps: no du/Sie alternation
gendered nouns for people: prefer plural or the Korean's own topic where nobody is named
trem/celular/banheiro/ônibus — not comboio/telemóvel/casa de banho/autocarro
estou aprendendo, not estou a aprender
camisola=nightgown: banned as sweater
full diacritics always
classifier choice per shipped rows
